plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid), so bidding your true value ensures you win exactly when the item is worth more to you than the price you'd pay, and lose otherwise - maximizing expected profit. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $39.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $20, I will bid exactly $20 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), which is strategically similar to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it maximizes expected profit. Since my value is $20, I should bid exactly $20. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable), and lose when others value it more (avoiding overpayment).
